_schema.description: Curated geopolitical event registry per docs/019_Geopolitical_Intelligence.md. Every event must carry sources (invariant: no unverified data). severity and oil_supply_impact are 0-10; confidence is 0-1. status: active | monitoring | resolved. Resolved events are kept forever (invariant: historical information must remain preserved).

events.description: Iran closed the Strait of Hormuz 2026-02-28; re-closed 2026-07-13. As of 07-19: third consecutive day of US-Iran fighting. Trump said he would reimpose the US naval blockade on Iranian ships only and demanded other transiting ships pay the US 20% of cargo value as protection; Iran is demanding all ships use a northern route through its territorial waters and continues attacking ships in the US-protected Oman-hugging lane. Transit refinement vs the 07-17 note: 57 transits were recorded Fri-Sun (>50% wk/wk drop, vs ~130/day pre-war), and DOE says 8.5M bbl still transited Sunday with military assistance (total Gulf flows ~15M bpd) — heavily disrupted but not zero. ~25% of seaborne oil trade transits this chokepoint. 08-05: SEVERITY HELD AT 10 DELIBERATELY. The physical state of the waterway has not changed - PortWatch's last published day (07-23) put commercial transit at 11% of pre-crisis volume, 10 vessels against a typical 88/day, and ship-tracking showed 8 commodity ships on 07-28 and 1 on 07-29. What changed is the PATH OUT, not the state: an interim reopening proposal is drafted (see us-iran-qatar-talks-2026) including mine clearing from the median lane within 30 days. Severity measures the disruption that exists; the probability of it ending is carried by the talks event, whose confidence rose 0.30 -> 0.70 today. Recording this explicitly so the registry is not read as ignoring the news.
events.update_log_0723: 07-23: escalation widened — reports of attacks on tankers OFF THE SAUDI COAST (beyond Hormuz itself) and Trump renewed threats to intensify strikes on Iran; WTI +~3.8% to ~$90.14 (highest since June 8), Brent ~$98.44. The escalation vector is spreading regionally.
events.update_log_0726: 07-26 (weekend): Trump warned that each Iranian attack on a ship in the strait will be met with a US strike on an Iranian bridge or power plant, possibly near/within Tehran — a new infrastructure-targeting threat; Iran responded defiantly. Transits still ~6/day (Jul 18-19). ~27% of seaborne crude/products transit the strait. Talks remain stalled on the Hormuz-control sticking point. Watch the Sunday 6 PM ET reopen for a gap.
events.update_log_0728: 07-28: THE CLOSURE ITSELF HAS NOT CHANGED — severity held at 10/10. Trackers put the strait at day 148 closed. Traffic averaged ~10 ships/day 07-13 to 07-19 vs an ~88/day normal baseline; 15 transits on 07-19; the tanker queue off Kharg Island grew to 24 vessels on 07-26 from 21. What changed is the CONFLICT tempo around it, not the waterway. This event is deliberately left at its headline severity and damped downstream by the realized-capacity factor — see the 07-28 chokepoint_status observation (32%, confidence 0.55). Do not cut this event's severity to express de-escalation; that is the capacity component's job.
events.update_log_0729: 07-29: no reported change to the waterway itself - the 07-28 escalation hit Jordan and eastern Iraq, not Gulf shipping or energy infrastructure. No new vessel attack reported since the Kaifan on 07-20. Severity held at 10/10; the 07-28 capacity observation (32%, confidence 0.55) still stands and is now 1 day old.
events.update_log_0730: 07-30: MarineTraffic recorded at least 14 commercial transits in the prior 24 hours (8 inbound to the Gulf, 6 outbound to the Gulf of Oman) against a pre-war baseline of ~120 crossings per day - roughly 12% of normal traffic. Severity held at 10/10. The 07-29 US strikes hit Iranian COASTAL SURVEILLANCE, DEFENCE AND MARITIME CAPABILITIES at Bandar Abbas and Kish, i.e. the assets Iran uses to threaten the waterway. Near term that raises risk; over a longer horizon degrading those assets could REDUCE Iran's ability to keep the strait shut. Both readings are live; neither is scored as a capacity change until transits actually move.
events.update_log_0731: 07-31 FIRST RECOVERY SIGNAL IN THE WATERWAY ITSELF. Commonwealth Bank of Australia estimates traffic through the strait has recovered to roughly 30-35% of pre-war levels, and oil rose only modestly on the session (WTI Sep +1.54% to $84.87, Brent +1.37% to $90.25) BECAUSE the flow recovery eased supply concerns. This is the first independent third-party capacity estimate we have had, and it corroborates the 07-30 blended in-house figure of 30% almost exactly. Severity held at 10/10 - the closure regime is unchanged - but the realized-capacity observation is refreshed to 33% with confidence raised 0.50 -> 0.65 and direction flipped to more_open. Note the tension with the 07-30 vessel count (14 transits/24h vs ~120 pre-war, ~12%): CBA is likely measuring volume rather than vessel count, which is the leg that had gone stale.
events.update_log_0801: 08-01: no fresh transit count over the weekend; the 07-31 observation (33% capacity, confidence 0.65, more_open) stands and is 1 day old. IMPORTANT REVISION to the bypass framing: Yanbu loadings are running ~4.0M bpd vs ~973k a year ago, which is the East-West pipeline doing its job - but Yanbu barrels exit via Bab el-Mandeb, now under Houthi blockade. The Hormuz escape valve is partially blocked at its far end.
events.update_log_0802: 08-02: still no fresh transit count; the 07-31 observation (33%, confidence 0.65, more_open) is now 2 days old and is the weakest input on the board. Nothing reported about the waterway itself over the weekend. Watch the 22:00 UTC reopen.
events.update_log_0803: 08-03: the US has SUSPENDED strikes around the strait and along Iran's southern coast on CENTCOM's own recommendation, with the commander assessing that Iran's ability to threaten commercial shipping has been weakened. The waterway itself is still closed and no new transit count is available, so severity is held at 10/10 and the capacity observation stands at 33% from 07-31 - now 3 days old and clearly the weakest input on the board. But the DIRECTION of travel has changed: the military pressure keeping transits suppressed is being removed at the same time as Iran's ability to suppress them is reportedly degraded. Both point the same way. A materially higher capacity reading is the base case for the next observation.

events.description: Active military conflict between the US/Israel and Iran since late February 2026. 07-27 MATERIAL DE-ESCALATION: the two sides HALTED STRIKES against each other over the weekend — the US paused its attacks starting late Friday and Tehran halted retaliatory strikes — amid efforts to revive diplomacy. WTI fell ~5% to ~$84.83 and Brent ~4.7% to ~$92.27 on the news. This is a pause, not a settlement: the underlying conflict is unresolved and the strait remains shut, but the active-strike tempo that drove the July premium has stopped. Severity and supply impact cut accordingly (9/7 -> 7/5). 08-05 HELD AT 5. Fifth consecutive day with no US strike delivered. Trump said on 08-01 the US was 'locked and loaded and ready' at high levels of military power and then agreed to cancel the attack in exchange for negotiations; he has since reiterated the demand for a swift Hormuz reopening and warned Tehran this is a last chance before renewed strikes. THE ESCALATION LIMITER, NAMED: US interceptor stocks. Nearly 80% of interceptors for key missile-defence systems have been expended and air-defence stockpiles are particularly depleted by this war. That is a hard constraint on sustaining another strike campaign against a state with Iran's missile inventory, and it is a material reason CENTCOM recommended ending the bombing. Also on the record: in June Trump announced plans to strike 'VERY HARD' including KHARG ISLAND and other oil infrastructure, then cancelled when final points of an agreement were approved - the energy-infrastructure line has been approached twice and not crossed either time.
events.update_log_0728: 07-28: THE PAUSE HELD A SECOND DAY. No new US strikes; Tehran halted retaliation against US allies. US ambassador to the UN Mike Waltz said Trump would give negotiations 'a little bit of room'; Trump said the US halted strikes at the regime's request and will resume if no ceasefire deal is reached. WTI extended losses ~3% to ~$80.11 (Sep contract), Brent ~$85.08-86.58. Severity cut 7 -> 6 and supply impact 5 -> 4: a second quiet day with no vessel attacks since the Kaifan on 07-20 is a real change in tempo, not just a headline. Caveat below in the talks event — Iran publicly denies negotiating with the US at all.
events.update_log_0729: 07-29 THE PAUSE BROKE. At 5:45 PM ET Tuesday the IRGC launched multiple ballistic missiles from Iran at US forces in an 'attempted surprise attack' (CENTCOM), targeting Muwaffaq Salti Air Base in JORDAN. All missiles were intercepted; no US deaths. The launch came roughly two hours after Netanyahu left a closed-door White House meeting with Trump - their first face-to-face since the war began 02-28. Separately, US and Saudi aircraft struck logistics and weapons sites across eastern Iraq. WTI reversed +4.4% to ~$82.73. The 48-hour pause reported 07-27/07-28 is over: severity 6 -> 8, supply impact 4 -> 6. Note this attack widened the geography again (Jordan, Iraq) without yet touching Gulf energy infrastructure.
events.update_log_0729_airdefense: 07-29 NEW STRUCTURAL RISK - interceptor depletion. Analysis reported 07-28 puts US Patriot stocks at 759-827, down from 2,330 pre-war (-65%), and THAAD at 234-278 from 452. US forces are now reported to be DELIBERATELY LETTING SOME IRANIAN MISSILES THROUGH where a strike is judged not to threaten American lives. CSIS estimates three years to replenish. This does not change today's supply picture but it materially fattens the left tail: the probability that a future Iranian salvo actually lands on energy infrastructure rises as the shield thins. Tracked as a risk driver, not scored as a supply disruption.
events.update_log_0730: 07-30 THE US RETALIATED - HEAVY WAVE. Trump said it was 'our turn'; CENTCOM completed a heavy wave of strikes at ~10 PM ET on 07-29 against DOZENS of IRGC targets: military command centres, missile and drone facilities, and - the part that matters for oil - COASTAL SURVEILLANCE AND DEFENCE SITES AND MARITIME CAPABILITIES. Explosions reported across southern Iran including BANDAR ABBAS and KISH ISLAND, both directly on the Strait of Hormuz. Jordan's military said it intercepted five of the Iranian missiles fired 07-28. Brent jumped ~7% to $90.66 on Trump's retaliation threat. Severity 6 -> 9, supply impact 4 -> 7. This is the highest tempo since the 07-23 peak.
events.update_log_0730_energy_restraint: 07-30 KEY RESTRAINT, EXPLICITLY SOURCED: Israel's Defence Minister said the US has been PREVENTING Israel from striking Iranian energy infrastructure over economic and energy concerns, and CENTCOM's 07-29 wave targeted military and IRGC positions - NOT energy infrastructure. This is the single most important bullish-tail limiter on the board: the escalation is severe but is being deliberately steered away from the barrels. If that restraint breaks, the escalation scenario repricing is immediate and large.
events.update_log_0731: 07-31: no new strike round reported overnight after the 07-29 US retaliation wave. The policy vector shifted to ECONOMIC: Trump wants Congress to add tariffs on Iran to the bipartisan Russia/Iran sanctions bill (reported 07-30). Analysts note the direct effect is minimal because the US imports almost nothing from Iran; the live question is the separate 25% secondary-tariff threat on countries trading with Iran, announced 01-12 and still without published implementation guidance. Iran exports ~1.3M bpd of crude, almost all to China, plus refined products to the UAE, Turkey, Iraq, India and Pakistan. Severity cut 9 -> 8 and supply impact held at 7: one quiet night is a tempo change, not a resolution, and sanctions escalation is a supply risk in its own right.
events.update_log_0801: 08-01 (Saturday, market closed): no new US-Iran strike round reported over Friday night. Severity held at 8. WTI ended the week near $84 after an $8+ weekly range and finished July up roughly a fifth; Brent settled around $86-89 and gained more than 20% on the month. Two escalation vectors OUTSIDE the Iran file moved instead and are now logged separately: the Houthi blockade of Saudi shipping at Bab el-Mandeb, and Ukraine's strike on Lukoil's Volgograd refinery. Trump's statement that the US will hold IRAN responsible for Houthi attacks is the thread tying the first of those back to this event.
events.update_log_0802: 08-02 (Sunday, pre-reopen): ESCALATION IS TELEGRAPHED, NOT YET DELIVERED. Reports on 08-01 say the US is planning fresh strikes on Iran AS SOON AS THIS WEEKEND; the scope was not clear and officials cautioned they could still be called off. Trump at a Friday Cabinet meeting: 'We will be hitting them very hard.' Separately the State Department and US embassies in ELEVEN countries - Bahrain, Egypt, Iraq, Israel, Jordan, Kuwait, Lebanon, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the UAE - told Americans to consider departing or be prepared to depart, citing potential for 'unforeseen escalation' and Iran's willingness to hit areas not previously targeted. That is the strongest civilian-posture signal of the war so far. Severity raised 8 -> 9 on the telegraphed strike plus the eleven-country advisory; supply impact held at 7 because nothing has been hit yet. Traders should expect the 22:00 UTC reopen to price this.
events.update_log_0803: 08-03 MAJOR DE-ESCALATION - THE STRIKES WERE CALLED OFF AND THE HORMUZ CAMPAIGN IS BEING WOUND DOWN. Three linked developments: (1) Trump ANNOUNCED THE CANCELLATION of the planned weekend strikes on Saturday, saying Iran and 'other Middle Eastern countries' asked him to hold off; he had spoken with the Saudi crown prince, who raised concerns about new US attacks. (2) Adm. Brad Cooper, the top US commander in the Middle East, RECOMMENDED ENDING THE BOMBING CAMPAIGN around the Strait of Hormuz after concluding it had reached the limits of its effectiveness. (3) Acting on that advice, Trump on FRIDAY suspended strikes targeting Iranian positions along Iran's southern coast and around the strait. Severity cut 9 -> 5 and supply impact 7 -> 4. This is the largest single de-escalation step of the crisis and it explains the ~6% overnight fall in WTI to $79.54, which had been unexplained in the 08-03 macro report.
events.update_log_0803_centcom_assessment: 08-03 THE ASSESSMENT THAT MATTERS FOR SUPPLY: Cooper advised the Pentagon and White House that TWO WEEKS OF SUSTAINED AIRSTRIKES HAD WEAKENED IRAN'S ABILITY TO THREATEN COMMERCIAL SHIPPING. This directly confirms the two-sided reading logged on 07-30, when the US struck coastal surveillance, coastal defence and maritime capabilities at Bandar Abbas and Kish: near term it raised risk, but degrading those assets reduces Iran's capacity to keep the strait shut. The commander on the ground has now said so explicitly. This is a structurally BEARISH datapoint for the Hormuz premium and should be treated as the leading indicator for the capacity component - expect transit counts to improve from here unless the campaign restarts.

events.description: De-escalation diplomacy has shifted to Muscat: an Iranian delegation led by FM Araghchi visited Oman for talks on reopening the strait; France and Britain are studying Omani-drafted proposals for IMO-supervised navigational fees. Mediation channels are strained (Oman and Qatar both struck by Iran on 2026-07-12; Pakistan track suspended). Headlines around these talks whipsaw prices in both directions. 07-20: first de-escalation flicker — Iran said US talks 'could be pursued based on national interests,' and oil erased gains. 07-22 REVERSAL: the flicker died — Secretary of State Rubio said Iran is 'not serious' about peace talks and oil jumped ~4% (WTI to ~$87-88); it is now the 11th consecutive night of US strikes on Iran, and the toll/fee dispute over transit vessels is the stated sticking point. Talks path deteriorated, not advanced. 08-04 SPLIT TRACK: the US-Iran bilateral channel deteriorated sharply while a separate Omani channel opened. Less than 24 hours after voicing optimism that a deal was close to reopen the strait, Trump posted on Truth Social that 'Iranian Leadership is unbelievably duplicitous!' after Tehran publicly DENIED that talks had resumed (08-02/08-03). Iran's position: it is not talking to the United States, but IS talking to Oman about a NEW Strait of Hormuz route. That maps onto the two-corridor structure now reported in the strait - a northern corridor controlled by Iran outside the traditional Traffic Separation Scheme and still assessed as likely mined, and a southern corridor in Omani waters transited under US guidance. Read: the bilateral track is worse than yesterday, the technical/mediated track is better. Confidence cut 0.40 -> 0.30 on the bilateral denial. 08-05 BREAKTHROUGH - the largest single improvement in this event since it was opened. Qatar said on 08-04 that an INTERIM PROPOSAL HAS BEEN DRAFTED, and both Washington and Tehran signalled progress; Trump discussed de-escalation directly with Qatar's Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al-Thani by phone on 08-04 and said the talks are going well. TERMS AS REPORTED: (1) an initial 60-DAY arrangement, extendable; (2) a TWO-LANE traffic scheme - inbound vessels use a northern lane through Iranian waters, outbound vessels a southern lane through Omani waters, coordinated with Iran; (3) NO TOLLS OR FEES during the temporary period - this is the concession that matters, because the transit-fee dispute has been the stated sticking point since 07-22; (4) NAVAL MINES CLEARED FROM THE MEDIAN LANE WITHIN 30 DAYS, with Iran reported to be considering allowing European countries to do the clearing. MEDIATION: Pakistan is exchanging messages between Washington and Tehran - the Pakistan track, logged as SUSPENDED earlier in this crisis, has been revived - with Qatar and Oman both assisting. Confidence raised 0.30 -> 0.70, the highest this event has carried. CAVEAT KEPT ON THE RECORD: a drafted proposal is not a signed one, Iran still insists on controlling maritime traffic through the strait, and Trump has framed this as Tehran's last chance before renewed strikes. 08-05 MIDDAY UPDATE - the deal moved from 'drafted' to 'imminent'. TREASURY SECRETARY SCOTT BESSENT told CNBC an agreement may come 'TODAY OR TOMORROW'. Iran is reported to be considering allowing EUROPEAN NATIONS to remove the mines - described in reporting as a climbdown. Scope is broader than the strait: the agreement is intended to (a) RESTORE THE JUNE 17 CEASEFIRE between Washington and Tehran, (b) resolve the shipping disputes over the waterway, and (c) create space for broader negotiations on Iran's NUCLEAR PROGRAMME. Confidence raised 0.70 -> 0.80. TWO CAVEATS KEPT ON THE RECORD, both from the same day's reporting: analysts characterise the emerging agreement as 'taking shape - but not one Trump wants', because Iran retains a coordinating role over traffic rather than surrendering it, and the deal is described as carrying 'a truckload of caveats'. A cabinet secretary predicting a signature is not a signature. 08-05 LATE AFTERNOON - the ROUTE is agreed; the DEAL is not signed. Iran says an agreement has been reached WITH OMAN on the proposed shipping route through the strait, and Tehran states the coordinates have been agreed. A JOINT TEHRAN-MUSCAT STATEMENT IS UNDER REVIEW AND IN FINAL DRAFTING; Iran's foreign ministry describes the deal as being 'finalised'. Axios reports the US aiming for a Wednesday announcement. Channel: several calls between Trump envoy Steve Witkoff, Iranian FM Abbas Araghchi and Omani FM Badr al-Busaidi - but IRAN CONTINUES TO INSIST IT IS TALKING SOLELY WITH OMAN, not with Washington. TERMS AS REPORTED: a 60-day temporary Oman-Iran arrangement, extendable, in which ARTICLE 5 commits Iran to using its 'BEST EFFORTS' to ensure safe commercial passage for 60 days, and Iran and Oman will 'define the future administration and maritime services' in the strait. Confidence 0.80 -> 0.85. THREE THINGS TO READ HONESTLY AND NOT SMOOTH OVER: (1) 'best efforts' is the weakest commitment language available in an international instrument - it is not a guarantee of passage; (2) Iran and Oman jointly defining the strait's 'future administration and maritime services' INSTITUTIONALISES an Iranian role rather than removing one, which is why analysts describe the emerging agreement as 'taking shape - but not one Trump wants'; (3) a route agreed bilaterally with Oman is not a US-Iran settlement, and nothing has been signed today. SEPARATELY AND UNRESOLVED: a vessel was reported struck in the RED SEA the same day - detail unverified at time of writing, logged so it is not lost if it turns out to be a Bab el-Mandeb escalation. NOT TODAY'S NEWS, RECORDED TO PREVENT A FUTURE MISREAD: the Trump-Pezeshkian 14-point MOU signed at Versailles during the G7 - reopening the strait, lifting sanctions, permanent termination of military operations, 60-day window to a final deal - is the JUNE 17 agreement, the one Trump declared over on 07-07. It is not a new signing.
events.update_log_0727: 07-27: diplomacy REVIVING — the mutual strike pause over the weekend was explicitly framed as an effort to restart talks. This is the #1 invalidation-trigger direction for the bullish thesis: if it firms into a reopening framework, the remaining premium unwinds. Not yet a settlement; the strait is still shut and no shipping-capacity change has been reported.
events.update_log_0728: 07-28 CONTRADICTION ON THE RECORD — read this before treating the pause as a peace process. Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei said Monday that Iran 'currently have no negotiations with the United States' and that its only official talks are with OMAN, about the future of the strait. Washington simultaneously describes the pause as giving negotiations room. Both cannot be fully true. Confidence in the diplomatic track is therefore cut 0.8 -> 0.6 and severity held: the strike pause is verified (observable, two days of no strikes), the negotiation is not. Treat the pause as a military fact and the talks as an unconfirmed claim.
events.update_log_0729: 07-29: the diplomatic read from 07-27/07-28 is INVALIDATED by events. Iran's own MFA had already denied negotiating with the US (only with Oman); the 07-28 missile salvo at a US base in Jordan settles it. The 'pause for talks' framing was Washington's, not a mutual process. Confidence cut 0.6 -> 0.4 and status held at monitoring. The Oman channel on the strait itself has not been reported dead - that is the only live thread.
events.update_log_0730: 07-30: the talks track is effectively dead for now. Iran fired first on 07-28, the US completed a heavy retaliatory wave on 07-29, and Iran's MFA had already denied negotiating with Washington. Confidence cut 0.4 -> 0.25; status held at monitoring because the Oman channel on the strait has not been reported closed.
events.update_log_0803: 08-03: the diplomatic channel showed its first real sign of life since 07-27. Trump's stand-down was explicitly framed as a response to requests from Iran AND other Middle Eastern states, with the Saudi crown prince named as having raised concerns directly. That is regional mediation actually working on US behaviour, which is different in kind from the Oman-only track. Confidence raised 0.25 -> 0.40. Still not a settlement and still no reported US-Iran direct negotiation.

events.description: Unidentified drones struck four tankers at the Caspian Pipeline Consortium (CPC) marine terminal near Novorossiysk between 07-17 and 07-20, suspending loadings for a week. Kazakh oil and gas condensate output fell to ~1.0M bpd by 07-26. RESOLVED 07-27: CPC restarted crude intake and tanker loading (SEAMAJESTY and MILOS loading Tengizchevroil crude at two single-point moorings); operations continue subject to security assessment. This is a NON-HORMUZ supply channel returning — a bearish input independent of the Iran file, and part of why WTI extended losses on 07-28. Kazakhstan produced 45.7Mt in H1 2026, -8.4% y/y; full-year target cut to 98Mt.

SECOND DISRUPTED CHOKEPOINT - added to the registry 08-01 after a review found it missing. Yemen's Houthis declared a complete maritime blockade of Saudi Arabia on 2026-07-20. On 07-22 they claimed a drone and missile attack on two Saudi tankers, ENCELIA and LAYLA; the Saudi Press Agency confirmed Encelia was hit, all crew safe. It was the first strike enforcing the blockade. Vessels are rerouting away from Bab el-Mandeb in growing numbers. Total petroleum transiting the strait was 7.4M bpd in June, roughly 7% of global oil output. Trump said the US will hold IRAN responsible for future Houthi attacks, which links this file directly to the Hormuz file. Saudi MFA says the Kingdom is taking all necessary measures to protect its ships. Houthis have not yet targeted port infrastructure. 08-04 DOWNGRADED 7->6. The blockade is being CIRCUMVENTED rather than enforced, and the Houthis walked back the escalation they had trailed. (a) On 08-01 the Houthis DENIED plans to charge ships transiting the Red Sea, four days after reports they would copy Iran's Hormuz toll playbook; the Houthi-run Humanitarian Operations Coordination Center states its 'safe transit service' is voluntary and free of charge. (b) DARK TANKER TRANSITS ARE SURGING at Bab el-Mandeb - tankers laden with Saudi oil are exiting the strait with transponders off, at least two confirmed in dark mode. (c) Saudi Arabia has re-routed part of its exports NORTHWARD to Egypt and the Suez Canal. (d) MARAD notes the Houthis have not attacked a commercial vessel since the October 2025 Gaza ceasefire, the 07-22 Encelia/Layla strikes excepted. IMPLICATION FOR MEASUREMENT: dark transits mean AIS-derived vessel counts UNDERSTATE actual volume through this chokepoint. Our 70% capacity placeholder was built on rerouting reports; the honest correction is upward.
events.update_log_0801_coupling: 08-01 THE COUPLING THAT MATTERS: Kpler and Signal Ocean ship-tracking shows Saudi loadings from YANBU averaging 4.0M bpd in recent weeks against ~973k bpd a year earlier. Yanbu is the Red Sea terminus of the East-West (Petroline) pipeline - i.e. it is THE Hormuz bypass route. Those bypassed barrels then have to transit Bab el-Mandeb, which is now under a declared Houthi blockade. The two chokepoints are therefore no longer independent: the escape valve for Hormuz empties into the second disrupted strait. This materially weakens the 'bypass capacity caps the Hormuz premium' argument that the 07-31 report used as the structural bear case, and it should be treated as a correction to that framing rather than an addition to it.

events.description: Ukraine's long-range drone campaign against Russian refining. On the night of 07-30/31 Ukrainian Defence Intelligence and defence forces struck LUKOIL'S VOLGOGRAD REFINERY - the largest fuel producer in Russia's Southern Federal District, design capacity ~15.7M tonnes of crude a year, supplying diesel and aviation fuel to Russian forces in southern Ukraine. NASA FIRMS showed several large active fires. Cumulative effect reported: Ukrainian strikes have put MORE THAN 30% of Russia's operational refining capacity (45% of nominal) out of service. Added to the registry 08-01 - this is a PRODUCT-side supply event, not a crude-side one, and it had been missing from the file. It tightens global diesel and jet balances independently of Hormuz, and it is a live reason distillates keep drawing. 08-04 ESCALATED 6->7. The cumulative damage is now visible in national throughput, not just individual sites: Russian refineries processed an estimated 3.6M bpd in July, THE LOWEST LEVEL SINCE MAY 2002 (a 24-year low) and roughly one third below the seasonal norm. As of mid-July refinery downtime and attacked capacity stood at ~4.3M bpd - about 58% of Russia's refining capacity - with an estimated 1.5-2.0M bpd effectively offline. At least 25 Russian refineries have been hit since August 2025, damaging crude distillation units, secondary units, storage, pipelines and logistics. On Sunday 08-02 Ukrainian forces struck the SARATOV OIL REFINERY (~7M tonnes/yr, one of the largest in the Volga region) and Engels Air Base, with fires at both. TWO-SIDED READ, stated plainly: this is unambiguously bullish for products (diesel, jet) and mildly BEARISH for crude - barrels Russia cannot refine are barrels available for export. The registry scores it on the product side.

THE ENERGY-INFRASTRUCTURE TABOO BROKE - from the Iranian side. On 2026-07-29 a drone struck the ENERGOS WINTER, a US-owned floating storage and regasification unit (FSRU, 138,250 cubic metres, owned by Energos Infrastructure) at Egypt's Mediterranean port of DAMIETTA. Fire spread to a second vessel, the GASLOG SALEM. No injuries. The Egyptian Cabinet confirmed a drone caused the fire; the New York Times, citing two Iranians, reported it was an Iranian drone attack, though there was no immediate claim of responsibility. This is the FIRST attack on Egyptian soil since the war began on 02-28 and it opens a new geography - the Mediterranean, near the northern approaches to Suez. The State Department cited it explicitly when warning Americans to consider departing the region. Severity 7, supply impact 5: LNG infrastructure rather than crude, and no barrels were lost, but the precedent is what matters.

US sanctions relief on Iranian oil - a sweeping rollback that permitted dollar-denominated trade in Iranian crude for the first time in over four decades - EXPIRES 2026-08-21. Added to the registry 08-04; it was missing, and it is the single largest DATED supply event on the calendar. Iran is explicitly maximising exports inside the window: crude and condensate output is tracked from 2.9M bpd in June to 4.0M bpd in July and an expected 4.2M bpd in August, with exports rising from a pre-war 1.7M bpd toward ~2.0M bpd. If waivers are extended, supply could push to 4.4-4.5M bpd. CHINA IS EFFECTIVELY THE ONLY BUYER: non-Chinese refiners have largely filled August-arrival requirements and the short window is too tight for their compliance reviews, so the barrels move at a discount into one destination. Enforcement against the shadow fleet has continued in parallel - the State Department took further action against illicit traders and shadow-fleet operators on 07-29 - so the relief is transactional, not a policy turn. TWO-SIDED AND DATED: bearish into 08-21 as Iran front-loads cargoes, sharply bullish after 08-21 if the waivers lapse and ~2M bpd of exports are forced back into the shadow trade.

chokepoint_status.summary: Transits collapsed to ~6 vessels/day vs 18-22 earlier in the month and ~130/day pre-war; US naval blockade in force and CENTCOM striking assets along the coast.

57 transits recorded Fri-Sun (~19/day, still >50% below the prior week) BUT DOE reports 8.5M bbl moved on Sunday alone with military escort against ~20M bpd normal Hormuz volume. Vessel-count and volume measures disagree (15% vs ~42%), so capacity is a blended estimate at moderate confidence.

First refresh since 07-19. Vessel-count leg confirmed and slightly worse: traffic averaged ~10 ships/day 07-13 to 07-19 against an ~88/day normal baseline (about 11%), with 15 transits on 07-19, and the tanker queue off Kharg Island grew to 24 vessels on 07-26 from 21 the day before - ships are waiting, not moving. The volume leg is unrefreshed: the last hard figure is DOE's 8.5M bbl on 07-19, now nine days old, so the blended 32% carries reduced confidence rather than a changed level. Military risk cut extreme -> high: no US or Iranian strikes for a second consecutive day and no vessel attacked since the Kuwaiti tanker Kaifan on 07-20. Insurance risk held at extreme - war-risk premiums have not been reported as repricing on a two-day pause. Supply impact bearish on the strike pause plus the CPC Black Sea terminal restart, not on any capacity improvement in the strait itself, which has not occurred.

Fresh vessel-count data: MarineTraffic recorded at least 14 commercial transits in the prior 24 hours - 8 inbound to the Persian Gulf, 6 outbound to the Gulf of Oman - against a pre-war baseline of roughly 120 crossings per day, about 12% of normal traffic. That is consistent with, and slightly worse than, the 07-28 vessel leg. The volume leg is still unrefreshed since DOE's 8.5M bbl figure of 07-19, now eleven days old, so the blended estimate ticks 32 to 30 with confidence cut 0.55 to 0.50 rather than the level moving sharply. Military risk restored high to extreme: CENTCOM completed a heavy wave of strikes late 07-29 against dozens of IRGC targets explicitly including coastal surveillance, coastal defence and maritime capabilities, with explosions reported at Bandar Abbas and Kish Island - both directly on the strait. Insurance risk held at extreme. Supply impact flips bearish to bullish on the resumption of active hostilities, though note the US is reported to be restraining Israel from striking Iranian energy infrastructure and the 07-29 wave did not target it.

First independent third-party capacity estimate of the crisis: Commonwealth Bank of Australia puts traffic through the strait at roughly 30-35% of pre-war levels, and the market traded the recovery as an easing of supply concerns rather than a squeeze - WTI September rose only 1.54% to $84.87 and Brent 1.37% to $90.25 despite the US retaliation wave two nights earlier. CBA's range corroborates the 07-30 in-house blended figure of 30% almost exactly, which is why confidence rises 0.50 to 0.65 rather than the level jumping. Direction flips no_change to more_open: this is the first time flows have been reported as recovering rather than holding or deteriorating. Military and insurance risk both held at extreme - no strike round overnight, but the 07-29 wave hit coastal and maritime targets at Bandar Abbas and Kish and war-risk premiums have not been reported as repricing. Supply impact moves bullish to neutral: recovering flows offset the escalation premium. Caveat retained - the 07-30 vessel count of 14 transits in 24 hours against a ~120/day pre-war baseline is about 12%, well below CBA's range, so the two measures still disagree and CBA is most likely weighting volume rather than hull count.

First observation for this chokepoint. The Houthis declared a complete maritime blockade of Saudi Arabia on 07-20 and enforced it once, on 07-22, striking the tankers Encelia and Layla with drones and missiles; the Saudi Press Agency confirmed Encelia was hit with all crew safe. FDD reports a growing number of vessels rerouting to avoid Bab el-Mandeb. Crucially the Houthis have NOT yet targeted vessels or port infrastructure beyond that single action, so this is a declared blockade only partially enforced rather than a closure. Total petroleum transiting was 7.4M bpd in June, about 7% of global output. Capacity is estimated at 70% and confidence is deliberately LOW at 0.45 because we have no transit count for this waterway at all - only qualitative rerouting reports. Treat the number as a placeholder that the damping should discount, not a measurement.

LEVEL HELD AT 33% - no fresh hull count since 07-30. What changed is the MECHANISM, and it is now documented: the binding constraint on Hormuz flows has shifted from military risk to INSURANCE. War-risk premiums for Hormuz transits are running 7.5-10% OF HULL VALUE, up from 1-3% only weeks earlier and roughly 0.25% pre-war. On a $100M tanker that is $3M-$10M per transit against ~$250,000 before hostilities; a single modern VLCC voyage can exceed $10M where the vessel, charterer, cargo or ownership chain is viewed as sensitive. Underwriters are withdrawing spot capacity. The strait is described as REMAINING PHYSICALLY PASSABLE while war-risk cover is 'one of the biggest commercial barriers to a normal recovery'. Structure: TWO CORRIDORS are open - a northern one controlled by Iran outside the traditional Traffic Separation Scheme, assessed as likely still mined, and a southern one in Omani waters transited under US guidance. Military risk cut extreme -> high: Trump suspended strikes on Iran's southern coast and around the strait on CENTCOM's recommendation (07-31) and cancelled the planned weekend wave (08-01); none have been delivered since. Insurance risk HELD at extreme and is now the reason the number is not recovering. CONFIDENCE RAISED 0.65 -> 0.70 - not because the news is better, but because we now have a mechanism that explains why flows stay depressed through a military pause. MEASURES STILL DISAGREE, FOUR WAYS: hull count ~12% (14 transits/24h vs ~120 pre-war, 07-30), CBA third-party estimate 30-35% (07-31), DOE volume 8.5M bbl/day vs ~20M normal implying ~42% (07-19, now 16 days old), and a Lloyd's List read of VLCC volumes down 36% with longer voyages implying far higher throughput. The 33% blend sits inside that spread and no single measure confirms it.

UPWARD CORRECTION 70 -> 78, confidence 0.45 -> 0.55. The declared blockade is being circumvented rather than enforced. (1) DARK TANKER TRANSITS ARE SURGING - tankers laden with Saudi crude are exiting Bab el-Mandeb with transponders off, at least two confirmed in dark mode. This means AIS-derived vessel counts, the only measure we have here, STRUCTURALLY UNDERSTATE actual throughput; our 70% placeholder was built on qualitative rerouting reports and was too harsh. (2) On 08-01 the Houthis DENIED plans to charge transiting ships, four days after reports they would copy Iran's Hormuz toll playbook; their HOCC states the 'safe transit service' is voluntary and free. (3) Saudi Arabia has re-routed part of its exports northward to Egypt and the Suez Canal - volume leaves the region by another door rather than being stranded. (4) MARAD notes no Houthi attack on a commercial vessel since the October 2025 Gaza ceasefire apart from the 07-22 Encelia/Layla strikes. Military risk cut high -> medium; insurance risk cut extreme -> high. Supply impact flips bullish -> bearish: more oil is getting through here than we credited. Confidence remains below 0.6 - dark transits are by construction unmeasured, so this is a better-reasoned estimate, not a measurement.

LEVEL HELD AT 33%, CONFIDENCE HELD AT 0.70 - and both holds are deliberate on a day of major diplomatic news. There is still no hull count fresher than 07-30. Today's third-party data is OLDER, not newer: IMF PortWatch's last published day (07-23) put transits at 11% of pre-crisis volume - 10 vessels against a typical 88/day - and ship-tracking showed 8 commodity ships on 07-28 and 1 on 07-29. Those corroborate the low end of our spread; none of them refresh it. THE CONTRADICTION OF THE DAY, STATED PLAINLY: the diplomatic path improved more today than on any day of this crisis - a drafted interim proposal, a two-lane scheme, no tolls, mines cleared from the median lane within 30 days - AND THE INSURANCE MARKET HAS NOT MOVED. War-risk is still pricing at 8.0x pre-crisis levels, 7.5-10% of hull value, with SIX P&I CLUBS HAVING WITHDRAWN COVER. Underwriters are not writing on a drafted proposal. Since 08-04 this platform has held that insurance, not military risk, is the binding constraint on Hormuz flows; today is the first live test of that claim and it passed - the military track de-escalated sharply and capacity did not move. Military risk cut high -> medium: sixth day without a strike, and US interceptor stocks are reported ~80% expended, which limits the capacity to resume a campaign. Insurance risk HELD at extreme. Supply impact flips neutral -> bearish on the reopening path, NOT on any measured improvement in flows, which have not occurred. If the deal is signed and mine clearing starts, the 30-day clock in the proposal is the timeline on which this number should finally move.
